newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Battered dlr struggles, Euro shares wallow.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Battered dlr struggles, Euro shares wallow.

text.p: The dollar struggled in early European trade on Thursday after tumbling by more than two yen overnight, while Europe's key bourses fell after a disappointing close on Wall Street.
The U.S. currency fell to around 115.60 yen in Asia, its lowest level against the yen since January, and Tokyo dealers said it was set to drop even further in the near term.
Top-level Japanese officials jumped in to try and stem the dollar's freefall, saying the Group of Seven agreement reached in April had filtered through to the markets "sufficiently".
Such comments -- made by Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka and Eisuke Sakakibara, head of the finance ministry's international finance bureau -- had their effect, pulling the dollar off its lows.
The dollar has now fallen nearly 10 percent from a peak of 127.47 yen on May 1, though analysts said a further plunge was unlikely even if the U.S. currency still looked sickly.

They said the dollar would proabably settle down for now, mainly because its value now seemed to be in an area which would keep both the United States and Japan satisfied. The slide had also been unsustainably rapid.
By 0915 gmt, the dollar had sagged to around 115.35 yen, however.

Behind the dollar's tumble overnight was speculation that the United States would support a stronger yen. Such speculation started in New York trade, fuelled by talk that a newsletter from a Washington-based consulting firm said Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin was calling for a dollar/yen rate of 115.
Subscribers to the newsletter contacted by Reuters denied receiving such a report.
Analysts said this was leading to a market consensus that a level of around 115 yen or slightly below was likely to keep the authorities fairly happy on both sides of the Pacific.
"The Japanese, for their part, don't want a really strong yen because of their export industry," said Adrian Davies, senior strategist at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull here.
"So basically there is a comfort zone that both the U.S. and Japan would be happy with, and when the dollar gets down to around 115 yen, the Japanese will say 'no more'," Davies said.
Meanwhile, the market was keenly awaiting a slew of U.S. data due late on Thursday for further clues on U.S. interest rates.

April consumer prices at 1230 GMT would be the highlight, as a bigger-than-expected drop in producer prices on Wednesday shocked the market and further clouded prospects of a rate hike at the policy-making Federal Open Market Committee meeting on May 20.

Elsewhere, Europe's leading share markets were all showing early losses. Investors were disappointed that Wall Street only ended 12 points higher having been some 52 points higher at the close of European trade on Wednesday.
In London, the FTSE 100 slid on profit-taking at the start and was down 20.2 points, or 0.4 percent, at 4,666.7 at 0915 gmt. The market, Europe's biggest, has stormed higher in recent days.
"The market has had huge momentum and is at its most technically overbought since 1989 and technically and fundamentally it is due some kind of consolidation," said BZW strategist, Steve Wright.
French stocks opened lower as investors took profits on the bourse's rally to record highs on Wednesday.
Traders said investors were feeling cautious ahead of the U.S. consumer price index.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down five points at 2,769.63, having picked itself off its opening lows.

Fresh polls showing the conservatives likely to win a majority of seats in the May 25-June 1 parliamentary election had little impact on the bourse. Traders say the market is unlikely to show much reaction unless polls signal a sharp change in sentiment.
German shares were also down in early listless trade as traders said the market was searching for fuel for a new advance on record levels. STOCK PRICES AT 0915 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was down 20.3 points at 4,666.6.
The Paris CAC-40 index was down five points at 2,769.63.
Frankfurt's DAX index was down 5.06 points at 3,568.63.
CURRENCIES AT 0915 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.6890 marks in late trade compared with 1.6977 on Wednesday and 115.35 yen versus 118.83.
PRECIOUS METALS

Gold opened $1.20 lower at $347.45 after closing at $348.65 an ounce in London on Wednesday. Traders said pressure came from a newspaper report that Germany wanted to sell Bundesbank reserve gold. But solid support was seen at $347.
